## Implementation Summary

- Change intent: the investigation-report mutation of the validator coverage verifier is derived from the instance under test, so check V4 applies it to any conforming report whatever option it recommends and however many options it evaluates, and always substitutes an option identifier the report never uses; with the unchanged run evidence the verifier now reports 6/6 COVERED with the committed investigation report caught by I1, and the mutation lookup and the V4 verdict are importable functions a test can drive.
- Approach taken: in runtime/verify_validators.py a new derivation `recommend_an_unevaluated_option` (rung 2 of the necessity and reuse ladder: it follows the six existing derivation functions and the table's existing callable-row rule) finds the `- Recommended option:` bullet, replaces the first three-digit option id on it with the lowest `O-nnn` absent from the whole text, and returns None when the bullet, an id on it, or a free id is missing; the investigation-report row of MUTATIONS points at it with check I1 and its description unchanged; the inline mutation resolution and V4 verdict of main() moved into `resolve_mutation` and `mutation_verdict` (rung 7: the analysis requires them importable, and no existing function exposes them), which main() calls with the same finding strings and the same checks-failed record; committed_instances and conforming_instance are untouched. One new test file (rung 7: no test of the verifier existed). The bundled payload mirror was regenerated by its sync command. No dependency was added.
- Design reference: root-cause analysis Fix Strategy (derive the investigation-report row from the instance, lowest unused option id, None on a missing field or no free id, keep I1 and the description, derive only with no selector fallback, extract the mutation lookup and V4 verdict from main() unchanged in behaviour, no validator, template, fixture, or run evidence change) and its Validation Plan (reproduction, new test file with the listed cases, full suite).
- Out of scope: the six other literal rows, which the analysis found pinned by their contracts; the selector functions committed_instances and conforming_instance, left as designed; every validator, template, fixture, and committed run artifact; the two count rows substituting 99, carried by the analysis as a residual for omn-tech-lead; running the release verification FR-02 in the main checkout or a hosted CI run, which the analysis routes to omn-qa after the fix.

## Deviations and Tradeoffs

| ID | Deviation | Design element | Rationale | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `V-001` | The every-row sweep in `C-002` uses the fixture where one exists and otherwise the instance conforming_instance selects, for the four types with no fixture (scope-definition, execution-plan, technical-design, framework-change-proposal) | Validation Plan: every MUTATIONS row must resolve against its fixture | Those four types have no fixture under runtime/fixtures, so a fixture-only sweep would skip them; using the verifier's own selector covers them at the cost of depending on committed evidence for those four subtests | not-required |
| `V-002` | The two witness tests in `C-002` apply the row through a test-local reading of the MUTATIONS table rule rather than only through `resolve_mutation` | Validation Plan: the first two tests fail before the fix and pass after | Calling the new function alone would fail on the pre-fix file by a missing attribute rather than by the defect; reading the row by the table's declared rule makes the pre-fix failure the defect itself (no anchor; mutation accepted), while the other twelve tests drive the extracted functions | not-required |
| `V-003` | `recommend_an_unevaluated_option` in `C-001` also returns None when the bullet carries no three-digit option id, and replaces the id token whether or not it is backticked, keeping the surrounding text | Fix Strategy: substitute one backticked three-digit id; None on a missing field or no free id | A bullet with no id gives nothing to substitute, and V4 then reports the missing anchor loudly as for a missing field; replacing only the id token keeps backticks and any trailing text, so the edit stays a single surgical change | not-required |

## Boundary Compliance

- Module boundaries preserved: the verifier still only reads run evidence, fixtures, and registries and writes its mutated copies to a temporary directory; no validator, template, fixture, selector, or other mutation row changed; main() keeps its six checks, output text, finding strings, and json-out record schema validator-coverage.v1; the test builds every instance in a temporary directory and writes nothing under the repository.
- Public interface changes: three new module-level functions in the verifier (`recommend_an_unevaluated_option`, `resolve_mutation`, `mutation_verdict`); the investigation-report MUTATIONS row changed from a literal pair to a callable row with the same check and description; the command line is unchanged.
- Data or migration impact: none; no schema, store, or run evidence format changed, and the json-out record keeps its schema
- Declared side effects: the three Change Set files, plus this artifact at runs/run-d8937789961e/states/fix-implementation/artifacts/implementation-report.md and the result envelope at runs/run-d8937789961e/states/fix-implementation/result-envelope.json. Both suite runs appended replay records to the committed run run-c5a8d50d3238, which were restored with `git checkout --` after each run; the run evidence of run-437e2f765e4b and run-d8937789961e was checked unmodified afterwards. The scratch copies and harness lie outside the repository; interpreter caches are not part of the change.

- Documentation impact: none beyond the verifier's own docstrings in `C-001`; the runtime README does not describe individual mutation rows.

repositoryWrites.scopePhasesRationale: This grant is automated test files only, and only in the `safety-net-establishment` phase of refactor, where establishing the safety net is the phase's declared output. Production source is never written in any phase, and this grant does not apply outside the one phase named above.
repositoryWrites.rationale: QA judges behavior, not code, so it does not author the change it validates. One phase is the exception the framework declares deliberately: a refactor cannot be validated at all until a safety net exists, and building that net is the phase's whole purpose. Even there the boundary holds, because a test that pins existing behavior is not the change under validation. Every other phase reads the repository and writes only its own artifact and result envelope.

determinism.contract: Identical inputs and an identical context snapshot must produce the same criterion result set, the same defect set, the same severity assignment, the same verdict, and the same declared report status.
determinism.orderingRule: Acceptance criteria keep the order of the source that declared them. Defects are ordered by descending severity; ties break toward the lower location in lexical order.
determinism.modelIndependence: No module may reference a specific model, vendor, or agent runtime. Technology names are permitted only when they trace to the supplied change, criteria, or repository context.
